headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels are documented, but B’s allowlisted egress creates a small leakage/conflict surface if operators bridge the pair manually.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented for godot_rl_agents or nuwa-skill. A has network_egress none and B only allowlisted egress, so there is no evidenced default path for A’s outputs to hijack B or vice versa.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A’s text into B’s prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added later, re-evaluate prompt trust boundaries.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw model outputs between agents.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared prompt buffer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows touched sensitive data, and A has no network egress. B’s allowlisted egress could transmit content if operators place sensitive material into its context, but the pair itself does not document a shared workspace or default data flow.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF B is given secrets or regulated data in its prompt, allowlisted egress may expose them to external services.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in either agent’s prompt.
Use separate, non-overlapping workspaces.
Review B’s allowlist before any run.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write surfaces, git state, or shared mutable resources are documented for either agent, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The only concrete asymmetry is B’s allowlisted egress, which could conflict with A only if an external orchestrator gives them the same mutable target.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state without locking, race conditions become plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Separate any writable targets per agent.
Add explicit locking in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic-concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented evidence that B treats A’s output as authoritative, and neither profile shows downstream action authority. Any cascade would require an external workflow that feeds A into B, so the pairwise pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited by the lack of action surfaces.
conditions: IF an operator pipes A’s generated text directly into B without verification, cascade risk appears.
IF B is configured to act on A’s outputs, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite or verify any claims from A.
Use a fixed schema for handoff data.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. A’s open-source game-playing profile and B’s scientific-research profile do not by themselves imply a residency or regulatory conflict.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF retention or residency policies are added to one agent but not the other, mismatch risk may emerge.
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Align retention settings if any are introduced.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging.
